title: Split-output handoff: SDK lab for progressive structured responses and tool handoffs
summary: Experiment PRD for a progressive, split-output response surface that lets hosted-api servers emit early structured frames for tool execution and partial UI updates while continuing to stream higher-fidelity content. Focus is on SDK ergonomics that make handoffs low-friction, observable, and resilient to network degradation.
goals: Allow developers to receive early structured 'action' frames (minimal tool inputs) before full text generation completes
Define a compact transport-friendly frame schema for partial structured output that is backward-compatible with existing streaming clients
Design SDK ergonomics for safe tool invocation, idempotency, and developer-friendly retries
Surface telemetry and trace correlation that ties partial frames, final tokens, and downstream tool executions into a single request timeline
Minimize latency for UI-critical signals (e.g., suggested actions) while preserving a single canonical response for auditing and QA
non_goals: Replacing full typed-tool contracts (this is additive: a lightweight early-signal surface, not a formal tool wiring replacement)
Building a separate RPC layer for tool orchestration outside the hosted-api (we will piggyback on existing streaming channels)
Guaranteeing identical semantic outputs between early frame and final text in all cases (we will provide guidance and best-effort consistency checks)
Supporting every legacy SDK in the first rollout — start with official JS and Python SDKs
user_stories: As a product engineer, I want the UI to display proposed action buttons immediately so my users can act faster while the model finishes composing longer context.
As an SDK consumer, I want a single high-level callback that can safely handle early action frames and the final content without writing complex state machines.
As a platform engineer, I want traceable signals connecting early frames to tool calls so we can attribute cost and failures correctly.
As an SRE, I want graceful fallback to traditional streaming if a downstream tool or client cannot accept partial frames.
As a security reviewer, I want explicit idempotency tokens and a minimal opt-in handshake for any automatic tool invocation triggered by early frames.
requirements: Server-side: emit 'frame' events in the existing streaming transport. Each frame must include: frame_id, frame_type, created_at, schema_version, payload (compact JSON string).

Frame types: 'action' (tool-invocation hint), 'meta' (progress indicators, estimated completion), 'partial_struct' (partial structured JSON that will be merged into final document), and 'final_snapshot' (canonical end-state).

SDK: provide a single API surface: onFrame(callback), onFinal(callback), with typed helpers: extractAction(frame), extractStruct(frame). Callbacks should be cancelable and support backpressure signals from the host app.
Safety: action frames that propose tool calls must include a required 'requires_confirmation' boolean; SDKs must default to 'false' only when developer explicitly opts in via handshake.
Idempotency: every action frame that can trigger a tool must carry an idempotency_key and origin_trace_id. Servers must persist minimal mapping for 72 hours to dedupe tool-side effects on retries.
Observability: frames must annotate estimated_token_progress and confidence hints where available. Servers emit a frame_trace_id that ties to request_id in logs.
Backward compatibility: if client does not implement onFrame, server must automatically degrade to streaming text only (no loss of final_snapshot).
Size limits: individual frame payloads limited to 8KB; total early-frame payloads per request capped (configurable) to avoid abuse.
Developer ergonomics: SDK should provide an 'action-snapshot' helper that synthesizes a small deterministic JSON for tool calls and a replay function for offline testing.

Security & Audit: final_snapshot must be stored by default for 30 days for customer audit unless retention overridden; all action frames that trigger tools must be logged with minimal user-identifying metadata per compliance settings.
acceptance_criteria: JS and Python SDKs implement onFrame and onFinal and a documented example shows immediate action button in <250ms after model starts streaming for a 512-token generation on typical p95 latency profile.

End-to-end demo: early action frame triggers a downstream tool (calendar API stub) and we observe a single idempotent effect in tool logs even with deliberate duplicate frames delivered by simulated network retries.
Telemetry: dashboards show frame_trace_id correlated with request_id and downstream tool call events in timeline view for sample workload.
Fallback: when a client opts out (no onFrame), final_snapshot still delivers canonical output and no early frames are required by the client.
Privacy tests: audit retention honors per-tenant retention flag and test tenants with strict retention show no stored final_snapshot after override window.
success_metrics: Time-to-first-action-signal (median and p95) — target median < 200ms on standard hosted region
Developer adoption: number of SDK integrations using onFrame hook in first 90 days — target 15 internal teams
Tool invocation error rate attributable to early-frame mismatch — target <1% of tool calls
Rollout safety: fraction of requests that required fallback to text-only due to incompatible clients — target <5% after 1 month
Observability coverage: fraction of frames with valid trace correlation — target 99%
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal SDK lab (2 weeks) with JS + Python minimal implementations and example apps. Phase 1: invite-only external beta with 3 customers for controlled tool wiring experiments (4 weeks). Phase 2: public beta with telemetry dashboard and opt-in config in Console (8 weeks). Phase 3: GA with stable schema v1 and console controls for retention and opt-in defaults (target quarter end). Each phase includes compatibility tests, performance profiling, and a kill-switch in the control plane to disable early frames per tenant.
open_questions: What should be the default retention period for final_snapshot for new tenants?
How aggressively should the server attempt to keep early-frame semantics consistent with final text when the model edits the proposed action mid-generation?
Do we allow multiple action frames for the same logical step, or should SDK coalesce duplicate 'action' frames automatically?
Edge: how to present contradictory early frames to the client UI? show newest, show highest-confidence, or show all?
Operational: size & state cost of keeping idempotency mappings for 72 hours — can we compress using bloom filters or verifiable logs?
dev-notes: Implementation notes: reuse streaming protocol extension header 'X-Frame-Schema: split-output-v1'. On the server side, emit small independent frames interleaved with token deltas. Do not assume frames are ordered by semantic priority; SDK should expose a stable ordering API. For JS SDK, implement a StreamReader wrapper that yields {type, payload, meta} and exposes a pause/resume/backpressure interface compatible with fetch streams. Provide a test harness that replays frames deterministically to validate idempotency and replay logic.
observability_and_telemetry: Emit events: frame_emitted, frame_delivered, action_dispatched, action_confirmed, final_snapshot_stored. Include fields: request_id, frame_id, frame_type, origin_trace_id, client_sdk, tenant_id (hashed), latency_ms. Provide a Console view that groups frames by request_id and shows timeline bars, with links to downstream tool call traces. Export CSV and signal to alerts when action_dispatched failure rate crosses threshold.
backwards_compatibility_strategy: Default to silent degradation: if client lacks frame handler, server streams tokens as today. New SDKs add explicit opt-in to automatic tool invocation to prevent accidental side effects. Schema versioning: include schema_version in every frame; support server-side feature flagging to serve 'legacy' mode for tenants who request it.
